newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai feedmills to push for more corn, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Thai feedmills to push for more corn, trade thin.

text.p: Thai animal feed producers were likely to resume their push for an extra 100,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn imports soon as local output is likely to be hit by lack of rain, trade and industry sources said on Tuesday.
In the local grains and oilseed market, buyers bought only moderate amounts of soymeal this week, all from Argentina.
"Most players were on the sidelines this week, waiting for prices to come down further," said a trader from US major trading house.
"A lot of supplies will be arriving early next month," he said.
More than 100,000 tonnes of soymeal were expected to arrive in the first two weeks of next month, according to shipping sources.
On corn, industry sources told Reuters that feed millers might submit a request for extra corn imports by next week.
"The industry expects domestic shortages this year and could submit the request by next week," said an executive from one major feed producer.
"We have to prepare to manage the stocks that we have. If the government says no, we'll have to turn to other sources such as broken rice and tapioca," he said.
The government earlier allowed the feed industry to import 200,000 tonnes of tariff-free corn. The amount was all covered and must be delivered by the end of this month.

Many players expect a bad crop this year due to insufficient rain during the tasselling stage in some areas. The agriculture ministry recently revised the forecast for 1997/98 corn output up to 4.53 million tonnes but feed producers and traders saw the projection as unrealistic.
Local corn price edged up to 4.65 baht ($0.18) per kg compared with 4.55 last week. Soymeal prices eased to 9.70-9.75 baht a kg this week from 9.80-9.85 baht a week earlier, trade sources said.
